blogs.title: Beyond Statins: Unmasking Drug-Induced Immune-Mediated Necrotizing Myopathy
blogs.description: This post explores the expanding differential diagnosis for necrotizing myopathy beyond the classic statin-HMGCR association. Using this unique case of semaglutide-triggered IMNM, we analyze why distinguishing true autoimmune myopathy from simple toxic rhabdomyolysis is critical. We discuss the 'smoldering' nature of IMNM, where symptoms progress long after drug cessation, contrasting it with the rapid resolution seen in direct toxin-induced injury.

blogs.title: Seronegative IMNM: When the Autoimmune Panel Lies Flat
blogs.description: Approximately one-third of IMNM cases are seronegative. This blog dissects the diagnostic dilemma faced when standard myositis panels (including HMGCR and SRP) return negative results. We review the specific histological hallmarks—macrophage-predominant infiltration, myophagocytosis, and membrane attack complex deposition—that confirm the diagnosis even in the absence of circulating autoantibodies, emphasizing the vital role of muscle biopsy in modern neuromuscular medicine.

blogs.title: The GLP-1 Paradox: Distinguishing Muscle Wasting from True Myopathy
blogs.description: As GLP-1 receptor agonists become ubiquitous for weight loss and diabetes management, clinicians must differentiate expected sarcopenia/muscle wasting from pathological myopathy. This article contrasts the clinical trajectory of this patient (progressive weakness over 4 months with massive CK elevation) against known cases of GLP-1 induced rhabdomyolysis (acute spike followed by rapid normalization). We outline a framework for evaluating new-onset proximal weakness in patients recently exposed to incretin mimetics.

blogs.title: Cardiac Involvement in Necrotizing Myopathy: A Silent Threat?
blogs.description: While skeletal muscle dominates the clinical picture in IMNM, this case highlights subtle but concerning cardiac findings, including elevated troponin/proBNP and MRI evidence of myocardial edema without infarction. We discuss the spectrum of cardiac involvement in inflammatory myopathies, ranging from asymptomatic biomarker elevations to fulminant myocarditis, and offer guidance on risk stratification and monitoring strategies for patients presenting with severe systemic myopathies.

blogs.title: Therapeutic Trajectories: Why Short-Course Immunotherapy Worked Where Others Fail
blogs.description: Idiopathic IMNM typically demands aggressive, long-term immunosuppression with steroid-sparing agents. However, this patient achieved remission with a relatively short course of steroids and IVIG after stopping semaglutide. This post analyzes the pathophysiological differences between idiopathic and drug-induced autoimmune phenomena, exploring why removal of the inciting trigger might allow for faster tapering and better outcomes compared to spontaneous onset disease.
